question:
In the Given figure A transversal line FD Cuts the Lines of AB at F, AC at E and BC at D then the Value of AF/FB × BD/DC = ?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c9d7fb83617191c9d255598082980db9d807b6ccdfea3512d1ffd32ef5c1ed9a.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By Menelaus's Theorem, if a transversal line intersects the sides of ΔABC at points F, E, and D, the product of the sectioning ratios is equal to 1.

⇒ (AF/FB) × (BD/DC) × (CE/EA) = 1

Rearranging the terms to isolate the required expression:

⇒ (AF/FB) × (BD/DC) = EA/CE

**∴ The correct answer is EA/CE.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A transversal intersects AB at F, AC at E, and BC extended at D.

**Construction:**

Draw a line segment BG parallel to AC, intersecting the transversal FD at point G.
